goal: Fix worktree-mode gated merges: relocate the untracked operator preview copies so they no longer collide with the canonical tracked files git brings, and make the merge path surface a pre-MERGE_HEAD git refusal honestly instead of attempting git merge --abort.

validationContract.statement: A worktree-mode gated merge lands the canonical tracked plan.md/report.md into the base branch while untracked operator preview copies are present, and those preview copies remain readable and are never committed to the base tree.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-engine --test merge_test preview 2>&1 | grep -qE 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

validationContract.statement: merge_no_ff, when git refuses a merge before MERGE_HEAD exists (an untracked-but-unignored file would be overwritten), returns the git refusal without running `git merge --abort` and leaves the working tree untouched.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-engine --test git_ops_test refused 2>&1 | grep -qE 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

validationContract.statement: merge_mission surfaces a pre-MERGE_HEAD merge refusal as its own distinct report variant carrying git's verbatim message — never as a Conflict and never as a wrapped Err.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-engine --test merge_test refus 2>&1 | grep -qE 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

validationContract.statement: The runtime .kranz/.gitignore ignores missions/*/preview/ both when it is freshly created and when a .kranz/.gitignore already exists lacking that entry.
validationContract.command: cargo test -p kranz-engine --lib gitignore_preview 2>&1 | grep -qE 'test result: ok\. [1-9][0-9]* passed'

validationContract.statement: The entire workspace test suite passes.

Across all three worktree-mode twin-write sites (plan approval, mid-mission re-plan, mission report), every operator preview copy is written under .kranz/missions/<id>/preview/ — never at the canonical .kranz/missions/<id>/ path that the gated merge brings as a tracked file.

milestones.title: Worktree-mode gated merge tolerates operator preview copies

features.title: Relocate worktree preview twins to a gitignored preview/ subdir
features.spec:
CONTEXT: In worktree mode the engine writes untracked human-readable operator copies ("twins") of the deliverables into the PRIMARY runtime dir .kranz/missions/<id>/ so an operator can read them without leaving the primary checkout (the canonical, committed copies live on the mission branch). Today those twins are written at the SAME paths the canonical tracked files occupy (.kranz/missions/<id>/plan.md, revised-plan.md, report.md) and are NOT gitignored, so the later gated merge fails with 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'. Fix: move every twin under .kranz/missions/<id>/preview/ (a non-colliding path) and gitignore that subdir.

SCOPE / FILES:
1. crates/engine/src/paths.rs — add a public method `preview_dir(&self) -> PathBuf` on MissionPaths returning `self.mission_dir().join("preview")`. Match the existing style of mission_dir()/plan_md_file() etc. Add a small unit test near the existing path tests asserting it resolves to .kranz/missions/<id>/preview.
2. crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs — repoint the THREE worktree-mode twin writes to the preview dir (they currently write to self.paths.mission_dir()/<name> or self.paths.plan_md_file()):
   - approve_plan, around lines 951-960: the `primary_plan_md` twin → write to `self.paths.preview_dir().join("plan.md")`.
   - mid-mission re-plan, around lines 1222-1228: the `primary_revised_md` twin → `self.paths.preview_dir().join("revised-plan.md")`.
   - try_write_mission_report, around lines 3226-3232 (the `if self.state.config.isolation() == WorkerIsolation::Worktree` block): the `primary_report` twin → `self.paths.preview_dir().join("report.md")`.
   Each site already does `create_dir_all(parent)` before writing — keep that (parent is now the preview dir). Do NOT change the CANONICAL writes/commits (the ones committed to the mission branch via the worktree) — only the untracked primary-dir twins move.
3. crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs — `write_kranz_gitignore` (around line 4855): (a) add a `missions/*/preview/` line to the template string it writes for a fresh file; (b) CRITICAL — the function currently only writes when the file does NOT exist (`if !file.exists()`). Existing repos already have .kranz/.gitignore, so a template-only change never reaches them. Make it idempotent: when the file already exists, read it and, if it does not already contain `missions/*/preview/`, append that line (with a trailing newline). Keep the fresh-file path working too. Preserve the existing entries and their ordering.
4. crates/engine/tests/worktree_isolation.rs — the twin-readability assertions around lines 647-657 currently assert `mission_dir.join("plan.md")` and `mission_dir.join("report.md")` are files; update them to the new `mission_dir.join("preview").join("plan.md")` / `preview/report.md` paths. Grep the whole file for any other assertions or comments referencing the old twin paths (search for `plan.md` / `report.md` / `twin`) and update them consistently so the suite passes.

TESTS TO ADD:
- In crates/engine/tests/merge_test.rs add a test whose NAME CONTAINS the substring `preview` (e.g. `merge_lands_canonical_with_untracked_preview_copies_present`). Use the existing helpers in that file (seeded_repo, seed_mission_branch, passing_executor, raw_git). Build a scenario where: the mission branch (kranz/mission-x) brings TRACKED files at .kranz/missions/m-x/plan.md and .kranz/missions/m-x/report.md; on the base checkout, BEFORE the merge, create UNTRACKED files at .kranz/missions/m-x/preview/plan.md and .kranz/missions/m-x/preview/report.md (any content). Call merge_mission(&repo, "main", &seed, "kranz/mission-x", passing_executor) and assert the result matches MergeReport::Merged. Then assert: both preview files still exist and are readable after the merge; and `git ls-files` on the merged base does NOT list any path under .kranz/missions/m-x/preview/ (the twins were never committed). This proves the non-collision fix.
- Add a lib unit test (in the #[cfg(test)] module of orchestrator.rs, alongside the existing preview_config_patch tests) whose NAME CONTAINS `gitignore_preview`. It must assert BOTH: (1) calling write_kranz_gitignore on a MissionPaths rooted at a fresh tempdir produces a .kranz/.gitignore whose contents contain `missions/*/preview/`; (2) when a .kranz/.gitignore is pre-created WITHOUT that line, calling write_kranz_gitignore appends it (contents afterward contain `missions/*/preview/`) while preserving the pre-existing lines.

CONSTRAINTS: Do not add dependencies. Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -p kranz-engine` before finishing (a prior mission cost a full respawn because fmt was skipped). Run `cargo test -p kranz-engine` and confirm green, including the updated worktree_isolation assertions. Do not touch the merge_no_ff / MergeOutcome logic — that is a separate feature.
validationCriteria: A test whose name contains `preview` exists in crates/engine/tests/merge_test.rs: it places untracked .kranz/missions/<id>/preview/plan.md and preview/report.md before the merge, runs merge_mission with a passing gate against a mission branch that brings tracked plan.md/report.md, and asserts MergeReport::Merged, that both preview files remain readable afterward, and that no preview/ path is tracked in the merged base tree.

A lib test whose name contains `gitignore_preview` asserts write_kranz_gitignore causes .kranz/.gitignore to ignore missions/*/preview/ both when the file is freshly created and when a .kranz/.gitignore already exists lacking that entry (pre-existing lines preserved).

The three worktree-mode twin writes in orchestrator.rs (plan approval, mid-mission re-plan, mission report) all write under .kranz/missions/<id>/preview/, and the worktree_isolation.rs twin-readability assertions are updated to the new path.
cargo test -p kranz-engine passes and cargo fmt / cargo clippy -p kranz-engine are clean.

features.title: merge_no_ff surfaces pre-MERGE_HEAD refusals without a spurious git merge --abort
features.spec:
CONTEXT: crates/engine/src/git_ops.rs `merge_no_ff` (around lines 382-407) treats ANY failed `git merge --no-ff` as a mid-merge conflict: it collects unmerged paths and unconditionally runs `git merge --abort`. But when git refuses BEFORE starting the merge (e.g. 'untracked working tree files would be overwritten by merge'), there is no MERGE_HEAD and nothing to abort, so `git merge --abort` itself fails and the real refusal gets buried under the misleading 'conflicted and `git merge --abort` also failed' error. Fix: distinguish a genuine mid-merge conflict from a pre-MERGE_HEAD refusal, and for the refusal case return git's message verbatim WITHOUT attempting an abort.

SCOPE / FILES:
1. crates/engine/src/git_ops.rs:
   - Add a new variant to the MergeOutcome enum (around line 31): `Refused { stderr: String }`, documented as: git refused the merge before any MERGE_HEAD was created — the merge never started, so the working tree and index are untouched and no abort is performed; `stderr` carries git's verbatim refusal message.
   - In merge_no_ff: the failing `git merge` currently goes through `self.probe(...)?.status.success()`. Keep the Output so you can read stderr (e.g. `let out = self.probe(&["merge", "--no-ff", "--no-edit", branch])?; if out.status.success() { return Ok(MergeOutcome::Clean); }`). After a failure, determine whether a merge is actually in progress by probing MERGE_HEAD: `let in_progress = self.probe(&["rev-parse", "-q", "--verify", "MERGE_HEAD"]).map(|o| o.status.success()).unwrap_or(false);`. If NOT in_progress: return `Ok(MergeOutcome::Refused { stderr: String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr).trim().to_string() })` and DO NOT run `git merge --abort`. If in_progress: keep the EXISTING behaviour exactly (collect unmerged_paths(), run `git merge --abort` treating its failure as a real Err, return MergeOutcome::Conflict { files }). Update the merge_no_ff doc comment to describe the new Refused outcome.
2. crates/engine/src/merge.rs:
   - Add a MergeReport variant `RefusedPreMerge { stderr: String }`, documented as: git refused the merge before it began (e.g. an untracked working-tree file would be overwritten); the base branch and working tree are untouched, no gates re-ran.
   - In merge_mission, map `MergeOutcome::Refused { stderr }` → `MergeReport::RefusedPreMerge { stderr }` in the match on merge_no_ff's result. Do not otherwise change the sequencing.
3. crates/server/src/host.rs — the match on MergeReport in the merge route (around lines 609-618) is exhaustive; add an arm for `MergeReport::RefusedPreMerge { stderr }` returning `ApiError::conflict(...)` with a message that includes the stderr (mirror the shape of the existing Conflict/RefusedDirtyTree arms).
4. crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs — the parallel per-feature merge matches MergeOutcome around lines 2293-2306 (Clean / Conflict arms). Add a `MergeOutcome::Refused { stderr }` arm. This path is not the gated final merge; a Refused here means an untracked file blocked a feature-branch integration — handle it as an integration failure by mirroring the existing Conflict arm's failure handling and surfacing the stderr in the message/reason. Read that block and keep the arm consistent with how Conflict is treated there.

TESTS TO ADD:
- In crates/engine/tests/git_ops_test.rs add a test whose NAME CONTAINS `refused` (e.g. `merge_no_ff_refuses_pre_merge_head_without_abort`). Use the file's existing helpers. Set up: a mission branch that adds a TRACKED file (e.g. foo.txt) off the seed; back on main, create an UNTRACKED, UNIGNORED file at the same path (foo.txt) with different content; call repo.merge_no_ff("<mission-branch>"). Assert: the result is MergeOutcome::Refused and its stderr contains the substring `would be overwritten`; the untracked foo.txt still exists with its original untracked content (untouched); there is NO MERGE_HEAD (no merge in progress) afterward; and the call did NOT return an Err mentioning 'abort'. Follow the fixture/skip-if-no-git conventions already in that file.
- In crates/engine/tests/merge_test.rs add a test whose NAME CONTAINS the substring `refus` (e.g. `merge_mission_reports_pre_merge_refusal`). Drive the SAME collision through merge_mission with a passing gate executor: the mission branch brings tracked foo.txt, an untracked-unignored foo.txt sits on the base checkout (note: an untracked file does NOT make the tracked tree dirty, so is_clean_tracked passes and gates run). Assert the result is MergeReport::RefusedPreMerge with stderr containing `would be overwritten`, and explicitly assert it is NEITHER MergeReport::Conflict NOR a propagated Err.

CONSTRAINTS: Do not add dependencies. Ensure every match on MergeOutcome and MergeReport across the workspace stays exhaustive (host.rs and orchestrator.rs noted above; grep for other match sites to be safe). Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --workspace` before finishing (a prior mission cost a full respawn for a skipped fmt). Run `cargo test --workspace` and confirm green.
validationCriteria: A test whose name contains `refused` in crates/engine/tests/git_ops_test.rs sets up an untracked-but-unignored file at a path the mission branch adds as tracked, calls merge_no_ff, and asserts it returns MergeOutcome::Refused carrying git's stderr (containing 'would be overwritten'), that no `git merge --abort` ran (no 'abort' Err, MERGE_HEAD absent), and the untracked file is left untouched.

A test whose name contains `refus` in crates/engine/tests/merge_test.rs drives the same collision through merge_mission with a passing gate and asserts the result is MergeReport::RefusedPreMerge carrying the verbatim git refusal — explicitly not MergeReport::Conflict and not a propagated Err.

New MergeOutcome::Refused and MergeReport::RefusedPreMerge variants are handled at every existing match site (crates/server/src/host.rs merge route and crates/engine/src/orchestrator.rs parallel-merge match), and cargo test --workspace passes with cargo fmt / clippy clean.
